# Environments

Run production and non-production workloads on separate Vault clusters. Do not use namespaces or environment-based secret paths to separate production from non-production inside one cluster. The [static secrets management guide](/validated-designs/vault/administration-guide/static-secrets-management#antipatterns-for-kv-path-structure) explains why environment-based paths are an antipattern, and recommends a Vault instance per environment or, at a minimum, separate production and non-production clusters.

This page describes what production clusters require, how to tier non-production clusters, and which environment to use when you validate each type of change.

## Production environment

Isolate the production environment to ensure high security and availability. This environment is critical to business operations and non-production workloads must not affect it. Production clusters must fulfill the following requirements.

- **High availability.** Deploy the cluster as described in the [Vault architecture](/validated-designs/vault/installation-guide/vms/architecture), with servers spread across availability zones using [redundancy zones](/validated-designs/vault/installation-guide/vms/architecture#redundancy-zones).
- **Disaster recovery replication.** Pair the production cluster with a [disaster recovery secondary cluster](/validated-designs/vault/installation-guide/vms/architecture#disaster-recovery-secondary-cluster), placed according to the architecture guidance. Follow the [disaster recovery initial setup](/validated-designs/vault/installation-guide/vms/disaster-recovery-initial-setup) guide to configure it. Replicate only between production clusters, never between production and non-production.
- **Audit logging and access control.** Apply the existing HVD guidance without relaxing it for production: [audit devices](/validated-designs/vault/installation-guide/vms/architecture#audit-devices), [configure audit logs](/validated-designs/vault/installation-guide/vms/post-installation-configuration#configure-audit-logs), [authentication for people](/validated-designs/vault/administration-guide/authentication-for-people), and [Vault policies](/validated-designs/vault/administration-guide/static-secrets-management#vault-policies).
- **Namespaces for tenant isolation.** Use Vault Enterprise namespaces to give teams or business units isolated, self-managed areas inside the production cluster. Refer to [when to use Vault namespaces](/validated-designs/vault/installation-guide/vms/post-installation-configuration#when-to-use-vault-namespaces) for the recommended structure and antipatterns.

### Performance replication is optional

Performance replication is not a prerequisite for production. Add performance secondary clusters only when you need to scale local writes horizontally or reduce latency for clients in other regions. Refer to [performance replication architecture and setup](/validated-designs/vault/installation-guide/vms/performance-replication-architecture-and-setup#overview) to decide whether your workloads need it.

## Non-production environments

At scale, the platform team that owns Vault treats most non-production clusters as production. Development, test, and release pipelines depend on these clusters, so an outage blocks application teams and delays releases. Apply the same change control and availability expectations to them as to production. Only engineering or sandbox clusters, which the platform team uses for its own experimentation, can tolerate downtime and rebuilds.

Not every non-production tier needs its own production-sized cluster. The following table describes a typical tiering model.

| Tier | Purpose | Platform team treats as production | Mirrors production machine specifications |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Engineering or sandbox | Platform team experimentation with Vault features, configuration, and policies. | No. Tolerates downtime and rebuilds. | No |
| Development | Application teams build and test their Vault integrations. | Yes | No |
| Test | Application test pipelines run against Vault. | Yes | No |
| Staging | Release staging for application workloads. | Yes | Rarely |
| Preproduction | Final gate before production. | Yes | Yes |
| Production | Business workloads. | Yes | Not applicable |

Preproduction is typically the only tier that mirrors production machine specifications. Keep the Vault configuration, such as auth methods, secrets engines, and policies, consistent across all tiers so that changes behave the same way when you promote them.

## Where to validate changes

Validate every change in a lower tier before you promote it to production. Use infrastructure as code to promote the same change through each tier rather than reapplying it by hand.

Rows marked **(Proposed)** contain environment mappings that a practitioner has not yet approved.

| Change type | Validate first in | Then promote through | What validation includes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ACL policies and Sentinel policies | Engineering or development | Higher tiers to production | Policy testing in a low-risk tier, because a policy mistake in production can block access to secrets for business workloads. |
| Vault version upgrades **(Proposed)** | Engineering or sandbox, then preproduction | Production | Restore a snapshot of production data into a test cluster with external network connectivity blocked, so the test cluster cannot revoke real credentials. Run the [Vault Enterprise upgrade](/validated-designs/vault/administration-guide/upgrade-procedures#vault-enterprise-upgrade) procedure, tested by someone other than its author. |
| Integrations such as auth methods, secrets engines, and Vault Agent **(Proposed)** | Development or test | Staging or preproduction, then production | Refer to the human input note that follows. |
| Disaster recovery failover and promotion **(Proposed)** | Preproduction | Production | Follow the [disaster recovery operations](/validated-designs/vault/administration-guide/disaster-recovery-operations) guide. |
| Capacity and performance | Preproduction | Not applicable | Load testing on the tier that mirrors production machine specifications, typically preproduction. |

The snapshot-based upgrade test follows the <a href="https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/upgrade/replicated-deployment" target="_blank" rel="noopener">replicated deployment upgrade</a> documentation.

## Namespaces are not environment boundaries

Namespaces isolate tenants inside one cluster. All namespaces in a cluster share the same servers, storage, version, and upgrade schedule, so a non-production workload in a namespace can still affect production availability. Use namespaces for tenant isolation within each environment, and use separate clusters for environment isolation. Refer to [Vault namespaces](/validated-designs/vault/installation-guide/vms/post-installation-configuration#namespaces) for namespace design guidance.
